title: The Knicks Silence Says EVERYTHING: Is the Deuce McBride Era Coming to an End?

paragraphs.text: Sometimes it is not the moves a team makes. It is the moves a team does not make that reveal the future. And the silence coming out of New York last night might just be the first tremor of a storm that is about to hit in the coming months.
That is right, everybody. Today we are breaking down a contract the Knicks did not sign last night, and the master plan that decision is pointing to.

What is up, everyone? Welcome back to NBA Tunnel. If you live and breathe New York Knicks basketball like we do, do yourself a favor and smash that subscribe button. A huge chunk of you watching still are not subscribed. One click supports the channel and makes sure you are the first to know every time something breaks out of the Big Apple. Now buckle up, because today's topic runs deep.
As of Tuesday night, a critical date is officially behind us. The final day to sign Miles Deuce McBride to a contract extension. And what happened? Nothing happened.

According to NBA insider Stefan Bondy, Deuce McBride and the New York Knicks did not reach an agreement on an extension. When the report first dropped, we said, let us wait a few hours and let it become official. Well, those hours have passed. The deadline is gone. And there is no signature on the table.
So why is this such a big deal? Here is the key, and it is hidden inside the rule itself. If McBride agrees to an extension after this date, he cannot be traded before the February trade deadline.

In other words, if the front office had signed him last night, they would have slammed the door shut on any midseason trade with their own hands. They did not. And that means the door has been left wide open.
Now let us play a little chess. What do we know about Deuce McBride? He is entering the final year of his contract. That makes him an expiring deal. A player who can walk in free agency next summer.

If McBride were part of New York's long term vision, and we all know Leon Rose and this front office are among the sharpest in the league, the obvious move would have been to lock him up right now. This deadline would never have been a problem for a team whose plan was simply, keep him.
But the signature never came. And that whispers one thing loud and clear. The Knicks are heading into this season with Deuce McBride as a tradable asset.

Honestly, you can upgrade tradable to likely to be traded. Maybe even very likely. As the February deadline creeps closer, get ready for this name to be one of the hottest on every front office's phone line.

Do not get it twisted, though. This is not about Deuce being a bad player. Quite the opposite. Deuce is one of the peskiest on ball defenders in the entire league. A spark plug off the bench who changes the rhythm of a game, never hesitates to let it fly from deep, and ignites the energy inside Madison Square Garden.

This is not about value. It is about timing and roster math. The NBA is a ruthless business, and for a team like New York with a championship window wide open, every contract and every deadline sends a message. Last night's message came through loud and clear.

Now for the fun part. The team the Knicks need to call, the team that every ounce of logic in the basketball universe points to, is the Charlotte Hornets. Why? Because Charlotte has a full blown traffic jam at the center position.

Last season's starting center, Moussa Diabate, is suddenly fighting for minutes, because the Hornets stuffed their frontcourt this summer. They grabbed a young big in the first round of the draft, and on top of that they traded for Naz Reid, who brings legit small ball five skills to the table.

The result? ESPN's projections no longer even have Diabate penciled in as the starter. So on one side you have Charlotte with a logjam at center. On the other side you have New York, a team that needs frontcourt depth. Is this picture painting itself or what?

And look at the Hornets guard room. Coby White, Kon Knueppel, Grayson Allen, and a rookie fresh out of the draft. Four names, sure, but question marks too. Nobody knows what the rookie will give you, and trusting a rookie in a playoff race is a risky business.

Then again, Charlotte is not chasing a championship. Their goal is to win a playoff series or two. And I keep being told the East is wide open this year. Me? I think the Knicks are the best team in the East by a runaway margin. But fine, for today, let us play along with the wide open East storyline. In that world, Charlotte hunting a guard upgrade makes all the sense in the world.

The first package that comes to mind is obvious. Deuce McBride plus a couple of second round picks for Moussa Diabate. Clean deal on paper. But flip the coin. Charlotte's shooting guard rotation is not weak. It is actually strong.

Kon Knueppel might be the best young shooting guard in the NBA. And if you think there is a better one, drop that name in the comments, because I want that debate. Grayson Allen is a proven, savvy veteran. And Coby White has basically played like a shooting guard his whole career. A catch and shoot scorer more than a true floor general.

So the position Charlotte is deepest at is the exact position Deuce McBride would slot into. Deuce is an elite defender and a knockdown shooter, but the ball handling and playmaking you want from a lead guard have never been the core of his game. That is where the fit breaks down.
And that is why my favorite scenario is a different one entirely. Tyler Kolek plus a draft pick swap for Ryan Kalkbrenner. Hear me out, because this move is a flat out win win.

What does this trade do? One. Deuce McBride stays in New York. The Knicks make another deep playoff run with this core, and then either Deuce walks in free agency, or you flip him at the deadline for a first round pick in the twenties or thirties.

Two. You are giving up a player who is not in the rotation. I know Kolek is a fan favorite. Trust me, we love him too. But let us be honest. As things stand, he does not crack the rotation unless there is an injury or some out of nowhere trade.
Trading a player outside the rotation, plus a couple of second rounders, for a player who would be in the rotation? Folks, that is the definition of a no brainer.

Picture it. You move Mohamed Diawara out of that emergency third center role and lock him into his natural spot in the forward rotation, and you write Ryan Kalkbrenner's name into that third big slot. What you are left with is arguably the deepest roster in the entire NBA.
And we have all watched it happen these last few years. The teams making deep playoff runs, the teams reaching the Finals, are the deep teams. In this era of NBA basketball, depth wins championships.
Now, somebody watching right now is yelling at the screen. Deuce McBride is worth way more than one late first round pick. I hear you. But here is the cold truth.

The entire league knows Deuce is on an expiring contract, and the entire league knows the Knicks are open to moving him. As long as that is on the table, rival front offices will drive the price down. The lowball offers are coming. And if a deadline trade becomes a must, we might have to settle for the best of a bunch of bad offers.
That is exactly why the Kolek for Kalkbrenner route is the elegant play. It strengthens the roster while protecting Deuce's value.

So which big man would Charlotte actually give up? That is the million dollar question. Kalkbrenner is only entering year two of his rookie deal, and the Hornets may want to hold onto that cheap, team friendly contract, which would make them more open to moving Diabate.

Or maybe it is the reverse. They see Diabate as the future and put Kalkbrenner on the table. Either way, the equation does not change. Charlotte has a center surplus and a guard need. New York has a center need and a guard surplus. There is no way both front offices do not see this. That phone is ringing. It is only a matter of time.

If you made it all the way to the end, you are the real MVP of this channel. Do not forget to hit that like button, and if you are new here, subscribe so you feel every earthquake out of New York first, right here on NBA Tunnel.

So tell me. What should the Knicks do? Trade Deuce McBride, or move Kolek and protect that depth? And is Kon Knueppel really the best young shooting guard in the league? Let us battle it out in the comments. Until the next video, much love from NBA Tunnel. Peace.
